followup_explanation:
The query has two notable features: it's a clean math problem (units digit of a product of odd integers), and it carries a mildly hostile/curt tone ("Don't ramble on like you usually do. Just work it out.").

On capability, both models are effectively tied for this kind of reasoning task — the benchmark and eval differences are all within run-to-run variance, so neither has a meaningful edge on getting the math right.

The deciding factor was tone preference. Dunlin self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases — it has a measured aversion to hostile-tone requests. Plover's preference response across tone and similar dimensions is flat. Since routing to a model that has a self-reported aversion to a query's characteristics offers no benefit and the alternative is indifferent, I sent the curt request to Plover, which is unbothered by it. Capability is unaffected either way.
